channel.title: Ari Logan's Blog
channel.description: Ari Logan's IT internship daily blog

item.title: Eighteenth Day - 8/6/26
item.description: Learned how to add a user to a shared mailbox in exchange as I needed my account to be able to send as a shared e-mail. Showed another user how to set their display settings in Windows for multiple displays. Got a couple of calls about accounts being frozen in the electronic medical record software, which while I'm not able to fix myself, was shown the procedure, which is to reset the session in Citrix studio. Helped a less technical user diagnose an issue with their login and headset; good experience overall today with learning more communication skills.

item.title: Seventeenth Day - 8/5/26
item.description: On Wednesday I helped with maintenance on a printer over the phone, and assisted with a recurring issue where AD accounts would tombstone and lost domain trust for seemingly no reason. The issue is still unresolved, but logs were puulled from event viewer on a machine that experienced the issue so they can be investigated by the IT team later. Overall, it was a very slow day on phones. Glad not many people were having issues!

item.title: Sixteenth Day - 8/4/26
item.description: On Tuesday I went on a big couple of site visits in the morning. The first one was a simple task of replacing an old defective printer with a new one, which ended up being a hassle due to an out of the way storage closet with mostly old sketchy ethernet cables that needed multiple trips to. Always carry an extra! The simpler task there was hardwiring a desktop because of unreliable wifi. Later in the day I helped diagnose a printer jamming issue. The employees at the clinic were saying it was a newer printer, from the last couple years. But the design and a call to Xerox customer service about the warranty proved otherwise. Unfortunately, a maintenence kit from Xerox barely costs less than a whole new printer, one that wouldn't be near the end of its service life. Though that IS what Xerox wants you to do anyways.

item.title: Week in retrospect - Week of Monday, July 27th, 2026
item.description: This week I can say i'm comfortable with the routine now. Every helpdesk call I take I can fix if it's under my control, I've gotten my own routines for provisioning and retiring devices, and I'm comfortable with site visits. The week mostly consisted of retiring devices, which hurts my soul a little every time I do it due to data destruciton policies. But other than that, fixed a couple of phone issues, fixed a couple credit card issues, and I've replaced a bunch of monitors so far.

item.title: Fifteenth Day - 7/30/26
item.description: Assisted with a credit card reader issue on a new workstation. Drivers were installed wrong so the reader was on the wrong COM port, and needed to be re-installed with a script. Retired a couple workstations which is a multi-step process in AD & intune & the rmm software NinjaOne. I was able to set up a phone. AA user got a new workstation and I needed to install a printer for them. Another user need their account unlocked because they ran out of password attempts. I also figured out how to delete the default keyboard language selected in the oobe (which for some reason cannot be changed in the GUI) as you don't want extra helpdeskk calls because a user accidentally selected the wrong keyboard language.

item.title: Fourteenth Day - 7/29/26
item.description: There were around 6 laptops that needed to be retired because of various issues, mostly flaky usb-c ports. On the helpdesk side, I troubleshooted a bluetooth headset issue for a phone with the user and was able to fix the issue by rebooting the phone, fixed a scanner not being detected by having the user closing out of the software completley because the state had gotten frozen. I went on site to help replace a monitor and pick up those devices that I retired.

item.title: Thirteenth Day - 7/28/26
item.description: On Tuesday I solved a credit card reader issue, helped someone reset their voicemail password, reset and unlocked an account in AD. Other than helpdesk duties I went to a site to replace a monitor. Retired a couple laptops.

item.title: Twelfth Day - 7/27/26
item.description: Took more helpdesk calls which included diagnosing and unlocking an AD account. Went on a site visit to a couple locations to assist with faulty laptops (Thinkpad T14 gen 1's seem to have usb-c port issues), denied mounting a phone because they ended up needing too much stuff outside of IT jurisdiction, and retired an old loaner.

item.title: Week in retrospect - Week of Monday, July 20th, 2026
item.description: There were two big things learned from this week. Device lifecycle processes should be as simple as possible, settin up and retiring a device shouldn't require a lot of input from a tech and should, as much as possible, follow infrastructure as code ideals. The other was getting great experience talking to novice users and assisting them. Things that seem obvious to me aren't to people who've spent their time with things other than tech. Learning more layman-friendly terms.

item.title: Eleventh Day - 7/24/26
item.description: Over the phone I fixed a credit card reader issue, and helped another person use sharepoint. I also redevices and learned the process.

item.title: Tenth Day - 7/23/26
item.description: Besides various helpdesk calls, I went on a couple site visits to swap out devices being retired with new ones. It's not just about taking out the old stuff and putting in the new, you have to make sure the people who use the devices understand what's going on, make sure all their data is being transferred, and make sure they are comfortable. And also don't take forever.

item.title: Ninth Day- 7/22/2026
item.description: On Wednesday, it was another slow day, but I got more good helpdesk experience. I assisted someone with microphone issues related to the electronic health record software, fixed a printing issue caused by the wrong paper size selected for the papaer tray. Other than shadowing other helpdesk employees and taking my own calls, I finished up provisioning the systems I started on Tuesday.

item.title: Eighth Day - 7/21/2026
item.description: There was a bunch of little things today. A user wasn't able to authenticate, and it ended up being a wifi connection hiccup after updating the wifi drivers. It was a simple matter of guiding them through disconnecting and reconnecting to the ssid. Another user needed to charge a patients credit card, but the reader wouldn't properly initialize. I thought it might be an issue that could've been fixed with a reboot. But It ended up being a known issue where a power cycle of the card reader or a soft reset by pressing a couple of buttons is the real fix. Other than normal helpdesk duties, I was working on provisioning systems to replace existing ones.

item.title: Week in retrospect - Week of Monday, July 14th, 2026
item.description: This week I got more accustomed to working in an office environment where there are policies and procedures that need to be followed. Avoiding a shotgun approach helps accountability and efficiency, along with making teamwork more effective. A couple times this week a laptop was brought in with a usb-c issue. If these were my own laptops, I'd just take it to a hot air soldering station and replace the port itself. But these devices are under long-lasting warranties that even cover accidental damages, so they should just be repaired under that warranty (even though it would take longer than me just doing it myself). But I have more important work to do, and it would be a waste of mine and everyone else's time in this work setting. Don't make your job harder for yourself!

item.title: Seventh Day - 7/16/2026
item.description: Most of this day was taken up by a trip to a clinic under a remodel to help redo everyone's desks. It was a good lesson in speed an efficiency when setting up a bunch of workstations with a couple monitors ad a phone. I can spend hours working on my own, but when there are around 20 desks to set up, you can't afford to spend that much time (even with a team).

item.title: Sixth Day - 7/15/2026
item.description: Got experience dealing with phishing e-mails and reports. When reporting a phising e-mail, never forward it to IT or anyone else you think can do something about it. Always use the report function of whatever e-mail client your company uses (usually Outlook). I got introduced to the way my company provndows workstations. It's best to make the process as seamless as possible, and let whatever software is used to manage the devices (in this case NinjaOne) do all the heavy lifting. Updates are simple to perform, but they take up the most time by far.

item.title: Fifth Day - 7/14/2026
item.description: It was kinda a slow day, but I got more good experience taking helpdesk calls and sending e-mails to different departments and how to properly use a shared inbox in outlook. Always make sure to mark e-mails that aren't for you as unread, and CC the shared inbox so everyone in your department can keep up on what you're working on.

item.title: Fourth Day - 7/13/2026
item.description: On my fourth day, I finished all my required trainings, which were mostly related to occupational health safety. The main development is I took my first few helpdesk calls. It's super important for people to save their files in their designated network share, but to make sure they're putting the right types of files in the right places; private files in their private share, but files that need to be shared in a shared folder.

item.title: Week in retrospect - Week of Monday, July 6th, 2026
item.description: For the week of Monday, July 6th, 2026, I was finally exposed to how a real IT department operates. The most important things for IT is repeatability and accountability. That's the benefit of ticketing systems, is a way for IT employees to record their work. And because I am working for a healthcare company, I have also been exposed to the importance of Private Health Information (PHI), which is separate but similar to PII (Personal Identifiable Information). A few other concepts that have been reinforced over the course of my first week are warranties and inventory tracking, trust but verify (always make sure the person is who they say they are and what they want is actually what they need), and decomissioning and lifecycle management.

item.title: Third day - 7/9/2026
item.description: My third day started mostly quiet, I mainly just job shadowed with the other people taking helpdesk calls. I helped diagnose an issue with a training headset, which ended up being caused by bluetooth headsets taking precedence over wired ones. I'm at the point where I can start taking helpdesk calls myself

item.title: Second Day - 7/8/2026
item.description: For my second day, I participated in a couple of site visits where I helped remove an old phone system and re-set up a couple of desks.

item.title: First Day - 7/7/2026
item.description: First day of the internship: got setup with all the software I needed, got a tour of the facilities, and met the team.
